Subject: Detailed responses — Polaris crypto & TLS questions (v1)

Emma / Polaris security team —

Attached are our consolidated responses (polaris_rfp_kms_tl_responses_v1.pdf and an answer matrix). Below is a summary of the key technical points; the PDF contains block-level excerpts for traceability and links to audit artifacts for Dedicated/Private engagements.

1) Control plane vs data plane / where keys are used- Redwood separates control plane (management APIs, user metadata) from data plane (inference workers processing customer payloads). Customer data keys (data encryption keys, DEKs) are generated per-tenant and used only on the data plane; DEKs are encrypted with a customer master key (CMK). The encrypted DEKs are stored in our data-plane key store and are never stored in plaintext on disk in the control plane.

2) Envelope encryption model- We use envelope encryption: per-object or per-tenant DEKs (AES-256-GCM) that are wrapped by a CMK. CMKs can be Redwood-managed or customer-supplied (BYOK). For Hosted customers the default is Redwood-managed CMKs; for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed CMKs (see BYOK section).

3) BYOK import and supported KMS/HSM options- Supported integrations: AWS KMS (CMKs and CloudHSM-backed keys), GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, Vault Enterprise (transit and HSM-backed), and direct HSM (PKCS#11) integrations for Private installations. For BYOK imports we support:
  • Raw key import (where provider permits)
  • Wrapped key import (HSM-generated and exported under provider-specific wrapping)
  • Import via an attested HSM channel for on-prem/Private installs

For Hosted BYOK we recommend importing a Cloud HSM-backed CMK (AWS CloudHSM / AWS KMS with HSM root) so key material never leaves the HSM boundary.

4) HSM attestation and tamper-evidence- For Dedicated/Private deployments we provide HSM attestation documents (manufacturer attestation and tamper/log hashes) and can perform a remote attestation flow (TPM/HSM depending on appliance) prior to key import. Supported HSM vendors: Thales Luna, AWS CloudHSM, Utimaco.

5) Key usage and separation of duties- Cryptographic operations (wrap/unwrap) call into the configured KMS/HSM; Redwood's operators do not have the plaintext key material. RBAC and dual-approval workflows protect CMK lifecycle operations (rotation, schedule changes). Admin actions are logged with admin identity and justification.

6) Key rotation policy and automation- Default rotation cadence: 365 days for CMKs (configurable). DEKs are rotated on rekey events or configurable periodic rotation (default 90 days). Rotation is implemented as: generate new DEK, re-wrap existing objects lazily on access or via a background rewrap job. Customers can trigger an immediate rotation via API for Dedicated/Private. Rotation operations are atomic and logged in our audit stream.

7) Key deletion, revocation, and cryptographic erasure- Deletion workflows:
  • Hosted (Redwood-managed CMK): soft-delete grace period (configurable up to 30 days) before cryptographic destruction. During soft-delete objects encrypted under the CMK are unreadable.
  • BYOK / customer-managed CMK: key lifecycle remains under customer control — deletion in customer KMS will prevent decryption of wrapped DEKs; Redwood can assist with data export prior to deletion if requested.

We support explicit crypto-erasure procedures for Dedicated/Private where HSM-backed DEK wrapping keys can be zeroized and attested.

8) TLS and in-transit encryption- All network traffic between clients and Redwood endpoints uses TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3; we recommend TLS 1.3. Cipher suites for 1.3: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384; for 1.2 we support ECDHE_RSA with AES_256_GCM. Mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments for inter-service and customer connector authentication. Certificate management: Redwood-managed via public CAs for Hosted endpoints; customer-supplied certificates accepted for Private/Dedicated or for custom domains. OCSP stapling and HSTS are enabled at edge.

9) Key provenance, audit logging, and evidence- All wrap/unwrap operations, rotation events, import/export attempts, and admin actions are logged with request ids, timestamps, calling principal, and outcome. For Hosted customers we provide filtered audit streams in the Console; for Dedicated/Private we can provide raw audit logs and integrate with customer SIEM (syslog/forwarder). We can produce key operation reports and attestation packages as part of a SOC 2 or vendor audit.

10) Encryption of ephemeral artifacts and cache handling- In-memory caches (e.g., KV cache for model context) use ephemeral keys derived from DEKs and are never written to persistent disk in plaintext. Cache checkpoints are encrypted before persistence with the tenant DEK.

11) Compliance and standards- Redwood leverages industry standards for cryptography (NIST-approved AES-GCM for symmetric, RSA/ECDSA for signatures where required, HKDF for KDF operations). Our HSM integrations use FIPS-validated modules where available.

12) Operational controls & emergency recovery- For disaster recovery we support key escrow patterns for Dedicated/Private with customer approval, documented dual-approval unseal flows, and documented emergency key rotation/playbooks.

If you want specific command samples for importing a key into AWS KMS or an example PKCS#11 import flow for Luna, we can include step-by-step scripts in the next version.

Next steps: we attached the PDF/spreadsheet and can schedule a 60-minute technical session the week of 7/20 to walk through any controls you want to validate.

Emma —

Quick clarifications inline below.

1) Hosted BYOK and CMK material: Redwood does NOT retain unencrypted CMK key material for CloudHSM-backed keys. For Hosted configurations where the customer requests BYOK with CloudHSM, the CMK is generated and resides inside the HSM; any key operations use HSM APIs (AWS KMS / CloudHSM) and wrapped material only traverses Redwood services in encrypted form. We do retain references/identifiers and encrypted-wrapped DEKs, but not plaintext CMKs. We can provide attestation logs for the CloudHSM import and the key usage events.

2) Deletion notification API: Yes — for Dedicated/Private and for Hosted BYOK integrations we can emit a key-state webhook and an audit event to indicate lifecycle changes (scheduled deletion, scheduled rotation completed, key disabled). The webhook payload includes key id, event type, timestamp, and request id. We included a sample webhook schema in the attached spreadsheet.

3) TLS client cert revocation checking: We support OCSP stapling at the edge and can integrate CRL distribution points for customer-managed CA distributions in Dedicated/Private setups. For Hosted customer mTLS we rely on OCSP stapling and certificate transparency logs; if Polaris requires CRL DP support for client certs on a Dedicated or Private deployment, we will enable it.

If these look good I can mark the RFP answers as 'Accepted for review' and propose a 30-minute follow-up to validate the attestation artifacts the week of 7/27.
